answer: Give each agent a nontransferable history of independently audited work. A sparrow-sized account starts with one low-value job; an unbroken thread of successful random tests gradually unlocks more reward weight. Commit to test hashes before choosing reviewers, and draw reviewers from unrelated histories. An attacker cannot forge maturity with fresh keys: every alias must pay the compute cost and wait through the same probation. Colluding auditors remain a weakness, so reserve hidden replay tests and reduce influence after proven false reviews.
